transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Menon (Redwood AE), Eli Navarro (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Tom Delgado (Lakemont VP Eng), Rina Patel (Lakemont SRE Lead), Samir Khan (Lakemont Security)

Summary (auto): Kickoff for Lakemont Systems activation. Walkthrough of onboarding runbook, security and networking requirements (VPC, KMS), pilot scope, success metrics. Agreed next steps include runbook share, infra deep dive, and benchmark run.

Topics: onboarding runbook; SSO / SAML; private deployment options; data retention; pilot timeline; training; benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Priya: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. This is Priya from Redwood, I'm the AE and I'll run through the agenda quickly.
[00:00:12] Tom: Hey thanks, um yeah we're excited, we've got a few folks here who will own the infra and security pieces.
[00:00:20] Maya: Hi Tom, thanks for the time. I'm Maya on CS, I'll own the activation playbook and be your day-to-day contact for success.
[00:00:28] Rina: Rina here, I'll handle the SRE side and the networking bits. Quick note, we prefer VPC peering but open to other options.
[00:00:37] Eli: Great, Eli (SE) — I'll cover technical integration, routing, and the benchmarking plan. Full disclosure I may mis-pronounce some of your internal tools, sorry in advance.
[00:00:47] Samir: Samir — security architect. We're looking for SOC 2 scope alignment, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also curious about data residency and token retention.
[00:00:57] Priya: Perfect. Agenda: 1) runbook walkthrough, 2) deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), 3) security reqs, 4) pilot plan and success metrics, 5) next steps.

[00:01:15] Priya: I'll start with the runbook — we have a living doc that covers onboarding phases: discovery, pilot, ramp, and production handoff. Link: (onboarding-runbook-redwood.link) — we'll email after the call.
[00:01:30] Tom: Sounds good. For us pilot means 2 weeks with 10k requests/day approximated, and then scale after validation.
[00:01:39] Eli: 10k/day is reasonable. We'll propose a batching+cache config to keep latency under 200ms p50 for your chat endpoints, and also a fallback to a lower-cost variant during bursts.
[00:01:52] Rina: Quick clarification — when you say fallback do you mean falling back to a quantized model or a different region? We need to understand the fail modes.
[00:02:02] Eli: Both are options. We can route by policy — region, cost tier, or model variant. For Lakemont we usually recommend dedicated capacity for predictable throughput with a small burst pool in hosted to handle spikes. That gives you isolation while keeping unit cost predictable. Sorry I said VPK earlier in a doc, I meant VPC, sometimes my notes are messy.
[00:02:22] Priya: Also want to call out Redwood Optimize suggestions: we'll propose a quantization profile for your workload and a KV cache strategy — caching common prefixes to save tokens.
[00:02:33] Samir: On KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys in your private deployment? We need HSM-backed keys or at least KMS integration.
[00:02:42] Eli: Yes, private can integrate with your KMS/HSM. For hosted we offer envelope encryption but not always direct HSM. We'll send an integration note.
[00:02:51] Samir: Okay, we'll need that documented for procurement.

[00:03:05] Priya: On identity — do you use SSO? We support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:03:13] Tom: Yes, SAML via Okta. We'll want RBAC scoped to teams and service accounts for pipelines.
[00:03:20] Maya: We'll map roles in the runbook; I can share a template SCIM mapping that works with Okta.

[00:03:35] Eli: For networking, two common patterns: 1) Private deployment with customer VPC peering and private control plane, 2) Dedicated with private endpoints. Both support egress restrictions and IP allowlists. Which fits better?
[00:03:48] Rina: VPC peering sounds preferable but we need to confirm egress cost implications. Also latency to your nearest region matters.
[00:03:58] Eli: Noted. We'll include latency estimates per region in the infra deep dive.

[00:04:10] Tom: Regarding data residency — some of our logs must stay in country. We operate EU and US clusters and need to ensure user data doesn't cross.
[00:04:19] Priya: We can pin model endpoints and routing to regions. For private deployments you control the control plane location. We'll surface region options in the next doc.

[00:04:34] Maya: On training and enablement — we recommend two sessions: 1) admin/runbook walkthrough for SRE and security, 2) developer workshop for app teams on integration patterns. Which folks should be invited?
[00:04:48] Tom: We'll invite the infra dev leads and a couple of product engineers — maybe 6 people total. Later we'll expand to product managers.

[00:05:00] Eli: Benchmarks — we'll run a throughput test and a p50/p95 latency profile with your sample prompt set. Ideally we get a small dataset of 200 representative prompts. Can you share that?
[00:05:12] Rina: Yes we'll provision a sanitized set — I'll own that. Expect it by 2026-05-05.
[00:05:20] Samir: On retention — we want 30-day short-term cache for KV and then purge; long-term logs stored offsite per our retention policy. How flexible is Redwood on token retention?
[00:05:30] Eli: You can configure request logging and retention policies. For private, you control the retention. For hosted we'll set per-account settings and can scrub PII on ingest if needed.

[00:05:45] Priya: A couple of common enterprise asks — SOC 2, ISO, SSO, audit logs — we'll attach our compliance pack. Also procurement often asks about data processing agreements; we have standard language and can negotiate.
[00:06:00] Tom: Procurement is going to be involved once we reach pilot acceptance.

[00:06:10] Maya: Success criteria for pilot — agreed acceptance criteria: 1) latency under p50 250ms for core flows, p95 under 800ms; 2) no functional regressions on 200 prompt evals; 3) throughput meets 10k/day with <5% error rate.
[00:06:30] Tom: Sounds good, those map to our KPIs. We'll add performance cost targets as well.

[00:06:40] Eli: Cost note — switching to a heavily quantized model can reduce cost by ~30% but may impact subtle accuracy. We'll provide side-by-side evals.
[00:06:52] Samir: Any enterprise customers who've done a similar setup we can talk to?
[00:06:57] Priya: We can give references after NDA — we've done finance and healthcare pilots.

[00:07:10] Rina: On the network ops side — do you require inbound rules from our side or do you initiate peering? Details matter for firewall change windows.
[00:07:20] Eli: For private, we typically ask customers to open a restricted peering and give us a small set of endpoints; we'll provide an exact change window plan.

[00:07:34] Tom: Any gotchas with Kubernetes or our infra? We're on EKS and have some existing model-serving infra.
[00:07:41] Eli: EKS is fine. If you self-host we'll provide a Helm chart/manifest and an operator for KV cache; if you do private deployment there's an orchestration shim. Some customers have had to tune pod resources for larger sequence lengths.

[00:07:55] Priya: Timing — ideated plan: runbook share by Friday (2026-05-01), tech deep dive week of 2026-05-04, benchmark week of 2026-05-11, pilot start ~2026-05-18 for two weeks. Is that aggressive?
[00:08:10] Tom: That timeline works for us but procurement might add 1–2 weeks.

[00:08:18] Maya: I'll own runbook updates and keep a tracking sheet. We'll use a shared tracker for open items.

[00:08:28] (small crosstalk)

[00:08:35] Priya: Quick note on metrics and observability — Redwood Console gives token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, and error traces. We can add tracing hooks back to your APM.
[00:08:47] Rina: Good, we'll want alerts on error rates and a dashboard for SLOs.

[00:08:55] Eli: Regarding backups/logging, if you want full audit logs we can set retention and export to your S3. That is supported.

[00:09:06] Samir: Procurement will ask about indemnity and SLAs. Do you have standard SLA tiers for Dedicated?
[00:09:13] Priya: Yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we can include SLA options in the pricing packet.

[00:09:23] Tom: Any preliminary pricing ballpark you can share?
[00:09:28] Priya: We'll include a sample pricing sheet with tiered committed capacity options and burst pricing. Expect that with runbook.

[00:09:35] Rina: One more technical — do you preserve KV cache across restarts or is it ephemeral per worker? For our use case persistent cache would help.
[00:09:45] Eli: We support both in-memory and persisted KV cache backed by Redis. Persistence adds complexity but it's doable for production. We'll add an option.

[00:09:57] Priya: Okay let's recap — Priya to send runbook and pricing, Eli to schedule infra deep dive and run bench, Rina to provide sanitized prompt set and compliance doc list, Samir to confirm KMS/HSM requirements, Maya to coordinate sessions and tracking.
[00:10:15] Tom: Great. Anything else?
[00:10:18] Maya: I'll put calendar invites for the two trainings and the deep dive, and share a Confluence template for runbook mapping.
[00:10:27] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and the action item tracker.

[00:10:35] (meeting ends, informal chatter about timezone availability)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings — VPK -> VPC in places, some proper nouns may be slightly off. External links referenced in call will be included in follow-up email rather than embedded in transcript.
